implementation_notes: date-fns represents the interval as a plain object {start, end} and the operations as pure functions: isWithinInterval(date, interval) is inclusive on both ends (its implementation sorts the bounds and compares with >= and <=), while areIntervalsOverlapping(left, right, {inclusive}) counts adjacent intervals as non-overlapping unless inclusive is set. Effectivity is therefore a plain record with an Interval field plus a query that receives an explicit asOf; an open end must be modelled outside the library (your own end: null plus a normalising wrapper) because the helpers expect real Dates. Choose it where date-fns is already a dependency; the Temporal variant replaces it once the target runtimes ship Temporal.
pitfalls: isWithinInterval treats both bounds as inclusive, so two adjacent periods both contain their shared boundary date unless the model adopts half-open dates (start inclusive, end exclusive-by-one-day) before calling it.
isWithinInterval sorts the two bounds internally, so a reversed interval answers instead of failing - validate start <= end in your own type.

new Date("2024-01-01") parses a date-only string as UTC while new Date(2024, 0, 1) is local midnight: a boundary built the wrong way is off by one day outside UTC. Date objects are also mutable, so a shared Interval can be changed by a caller.

variants.name: Temporal.PlainDate bounds (date-only, zone-free)
variants.implementation_notes: Temporal separates date-only values from instants: Temporal.PlainDate is a calendar date with no time and no zone, comparison goes through the static Temporal.PlainDate.compare() because relational operators throw (valueOf is disabled), and the distance between two dates is a Temporal.Duration via until()/since(). Effectivity is then two PlainDate bounds - or a null open end - plus a compare()-based containment test, and the boundary bugs of the Date era disappear because there is no time of day to fall off the end of a day. Choose it where Temporal is available (shipped in Firefox, polyfillable elsewhere); keep date-fns while target runtimes still lack it.
pitfalls: Relational operators on PlainDate throw a TypeError rather than returning false, so a forgotten compare() is a runtime failure - and duration arithmetic (until/since) must be given an explicit largestUnit when months or years matter.
Mixing PlainDate with ZonedDateTime or Instant needs a time zone at the boundary; converting a calendar-date period through an instant is a silent off-by-one in non-UTC zones.

A polyfill plus a native implementation in the same bundle yields two Temporal objects whose values are equal but whose identity and calendars may differ; parse at the boundary and keep one implementation.
